question: Sapna invested ₹20,900 on simple interest, partly at 10% per annum and partly at 9% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 5 years, then find the sum invested at 10% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest and time are identical, the ratio of Principals is inversely proportional to their Rates.

⇒ P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 9 : 10

⇒ Total investment ratio parts = 9 + 10 = 19 parts ≡ ₹20,900

⇒ 1 part = 20,900 ÷ 19 = ₹1,100

⇒ Sum invested at 10% (P₁) = 9 parts = 9 × 1,100 = ₹9,900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total invested sum = ₹20,900

Rate for 1st part (R₁) = 10% and Rate for 2nd part (R₂) = 9%

Time (T) = 5 years for both parts.

Simple interest earned from both parts is equal (SI₁ = SI₂).

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
